briefs.headline: Chalobah says he wanted to be a Chelsea legend before the Como sale
briefs.summary: Trevoh Chalobah, the 27-year-old defender Chelsea sold to Como for 30 million pounds ($40.1 million) in the summer, told The Athletic he "wanted to be a legend there" after joining the club at eight and that "Chelsea means everything to me. I'm still watching the games, keeping in contact with the players and staff." Chalobah made more than 150 appearances and won two Club World Cups, an FA Cup and the Conference League; he said Como manager Cesc Fabregas reached out over the summer. Chelsea, 4th on 13 points, host Saturday's house derby at Stamford Bridge at 12:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Hannan's season ends with an 8-0 loss at Buffalo in the Region IV quarterfinal
briefs.summary: Hannan, the No. 7 seed, went out of the WVSSAC Class AA-A Region IV quarterfinal on Wednesday night as No. 2 seed Buffalo beat them 8-0 at Buffalo, according to a team-reported score posted on MaxPreps at 8:07 p.m. Wednesday; the box score lists seven first-half goals and one in the second, no scorers, and labels the match non-league, while the WVSSAC bracket, unchanged since Oct. 20, pairs the teams on that date in the single-elimination regional. MaxPreps lists Hannan at 6-6-1 with no further games and Buffalo at 12-5-1. No newspaper or broadcaster this paper can read had the match. Buffalo also won the Oct. 1 regular-season meeting 5-0.

briefs.headline: Mac Allister says Iraola fixed what was wrong in Liverpool's group under Slot
briefs.summary: Alexis Mac Allister told Amazon Prime after Tuesday's Champions League win over Villarreal, in which he scored twice, that "last year was a really difficult year for all of us" and "something wasn't right in the group. This manager changed it." He said Andoni Iraola has Liverpool defending man to man where Arne Slot, who won the title in his first season and finished fifth in his second, used a zonal system: "you have to think less but run more." He called 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha "amazing, he made the difference." Liverpool, 5th on 12 points, host Brighton on Sunday at 10 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Ravens' Jackson practices for the first time in 17 days before the Bengals game
briefs.summary: Lamar Jackson returned to Baltimore's practice Wednesday as a limited participant, his first on-field work since spraining his left ankle against Tennessee on Oct. 4, and walked into the facility with a limp; coach Jesse Minter said Jackson "wants to play. But at the same time, you got to be healthy enough to play." Baltimore has scored 116 points in 14 quarters with Jackson this season and 40 in 10 quarters without him, and since 2018 has won 11 of 13 against Cincinnati with Jackson and lost all three without him. The Bengals' own Wednesday report listed only safety Kyle Dugger (quadricep) as limited. Kickoff in Baltimore is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Crew lose the Open Cup final to St. Louis City on penalties after a 0-0 draw
briefs.summary: Columbus outshot St. Louis City 16 shots to three over 120 scoreless minutes Wednesday night at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field but lost the U.S. Open Cup final in a shootout, the first final decided on penalties since 2015. Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt, on in the 78th minute after Roman Burki took a knee to the head from Anass Zaroury and was taken to a hospital conscious, dived left to push Santiago Rodriguez's kick onto the post; St. Louis converted all five, Daniel Edelman last, for the first trophy in the club's history and a 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup place. Columbus was seeking a second Open Cup title. The Crew, 11th in the East on 35 points, host Toronto on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET.

result.note: draw; St. Louis City 5-3 on penalties

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati beat D.C. United 2-1 on Hadebe's goal from an Evander free kick
briefs.summary: David Doudera scored his first MLS goal in the 14th minute Wednesday at TQL Stadium, Kimito Nono levelled in the 38th after a VAR review, and Teenage Hadebe turned in Evander's free kick from close range in the 55th for his first MLS goal since September 2023, in a match rescheduled from Sept. 5 and played before 25,513. Evander's assist was his 16th in all competitions this season, and Nick Hagglund made a club-record 180th appearance and cleared off the line in the 24th. Cincinnati (10 wins, 9 draws, 11 losses) move to 39 points and 8th in the East, three above Red Bull New York and Toronto, with four matches left, starting Saturday at D.C. United at 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Lakers beat Warriors 127-105 as Kessler goes 12 for 12 in his debut
briefs.summary: Walker Kessler scored 26 points without a miss and grabbed nine rebounds Wednesday night in Los Angeles, the second-most shots without a miss in Lakers history behind Wilt Chamberlain's 14 for 14 in March 1969, after the Lakers traded a package of draft picks to Utah for the 7-foot-2 center. Luka Doncic, in his first competitive game since April 2 and his first as the centerpiece after LeBron James' move to Philadelphia, scored 28 in three quarters and banked in a half-court shot at the halftime buzzer during a running exchange with Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg; Austin Reaves had 23 and Stephen Curry 23 to open his 18th season. Both teams play Friday, the Lakers against the Clippers and the Warriors against Memphis.

briefs.headline: Timberwolves beat Heat 131-106 as Edwards scores 45 in Antetokounmpo's debut
briefs.summary: Anthony Edwards hit nine 3-pointers Wednesday night in Miami and joined Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan as the only players with 40 points in more than one season opener, after his 41 at Portland a year ago. LaMelo Ball scored 21 in his Minnesota debut and the Timberwolves outscored Miami 63 points to 24 from three, turning a one-point lead into a 17-point edge with a 23 to 7 run that bridged halftime. Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 35 on 13-for-19 shooting in his first game for the Heat before fouling out; Miami has lost three straight openers for the third time in franchise history.

briefs.headline: Ohtani will not need surgery and is expected to pitch in 2027, Friedman says
briefs.summary: Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday that doctors prescribed rest for Shohei Ohtani's left knee and right arm and that "I fully expect him to pitch next year," though how the two-way workload is managed is undecided. Ohtani had eight wins, two losses and a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts but did not pitch after July 3, hit .294 with 30 home runs through Aug. 18, then had 11 hits and 29 strikeouts in his last 70 regular-season at-bats as Los Angeles was swept by Milwaukee in the NLCS. Friedman said Dave Roberts' staff will return unchanged. The World Series opens Friday at 8 p.m. ET on Fox with the Rays at the Brewers.

briefs.headline: Angels decline Suzuki's option after the franchise's first 100-loss season
briefs.summary: The Angels said Wednesday they declined Kurt Suzuki's 2027 option after one season as manager, in which Los Angeles went 62 wins and 100 losses, 10 fewer wins than in 2025 and the first 100-loss season in franchise history. Interim general manager John Mozeliak said he will not stay as full-time GM in 2027 and that the new GM, to be hired once Stan Kroenke takes control from Arte Moreno in the first quarter of 2027, will pick the manager. Suzuki, offered a special-assistant role, told The Orange County Register the decision "wasn't a surprise" with ownership changing. The Angels have not reached the postseason since 2014.

briefs.headline: NFL fines Sirianni, Vrabel and Glenn $250K each over conduct toward officials
briefs.summary: A source confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night that the league fined Philadelphia's Nick Sirianni $250,000 for conduct toward game officials, and Sports Illustrated, which first reported the fine, said New England's Mike Vrabel and the Jets' Aaron Glenn were fined the same amount for similar conduct. The fines are on hold and can be rescinded with good behavior, the source said, as the league seeks to make a point to all coaches; it was not immediately known when they were issued or from which incidents.

briefs.headline: Oregon rules out Moore and Stewart for Saturday's game at Illinois
briefs.summary: Quarterback Dante Moore will miss a third straight game with the concussion he suffered in the Sept. 26 win at USC, and receiver Evan Stewart is out with an undisclosed injury, according to Wednesday's Big Ten availability report. Dan Lanning has not named a starter; Dylan Raiola, who threw the winning touchdown against Nebraska after replacing Brock Thomas in the fourth quarter, spoke to reporters Wednesday. Stewart was arrested early Sunday in Springfield, Ore., on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants, and Lanning said the matter would be handled internally.

briefs.headline: Kyushu basho tickets are sold out, JSA says, 17 days out with the banzuke due Monday
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's ticket page for the Kyushu basho (tournament), Nov. 8 to 22 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, says all admission tickets are sold out and lists its fixed-price resale service as the only route; the banzuke (rankings) is due Monday, Oct. 26. Enho, 32, the 167-centimeter juryo (second-division) wrestler who fell to jonokuchi (the bottom division) during seven tournaments out with a neck injury and regained a salaried rank in May, has married, his Isegahama stable said Tuesday on social media, Sanspo reported; he went seven wins and eight losses at east juryo No. 9 in September. In amateur sumo, Japan and Ukraine took nine of the 12 gold medals at the 27th World Championships in Baku, Azerbaijan, last weekend, the Japan Times reported.

prime.item: Day 8. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:52 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address (HTTP 200, PDF, pdftotext), made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The limit it sets for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, with a three-inch minimum shell length; it is unlawful to take oysters between sunset and sunrise, or from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:45 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, while its own footnote reads oyster season is Oct. 15 to March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation, and the proclamation is the later document. The division's proclamations index, six pages read at 5:50 a.m., lists SF-1-2026 as its only October proclamation on shellfish and carries nothing issued Oct. 21 or 22. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, with a footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff them; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, re-read this morning with pdftotext, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. The proclamations index, six pages read at 5:50 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation and nothing issued Oct. 21 or 22; the two issued Oct. 20, FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, are snapper grouper complex orders effective Oct. 28. The limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required under G.S. 113-174.2, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 21 days old today, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day. The division's proclamations index, read at 5:50 a.m., lists the harvest opening as FF-31-2026, issued June 25 and effective 12:01 a.m. July 1, 2026, and carries no later seatrout proclamation. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 21 days old today, has the trout scattered, a few on early topwater, the guides waiting on cooler water; Beaufort's thermometer read 65.1 degrees this morning, up 0.9 from Wednesday's 64.2.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day in private recreational fisheries. The proclamations index read at 5:50 a.m. carries FF-35-2026 of Aug. 21 on Spanish mackerel, a commercial harvest-period order, and nothing on mackerel or bluefish issued since Oct. 9. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 21 days old today, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one over 25 inches allowed per person per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day. The proclamations index read at 5:50 a.m. lists FF-16-2026 of March 13 on sheepshead and FF-23-2021 on spot creel limits, and nothing on either issued in October. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 21 days old today, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

going_out.dates: Harvest Sept. 1 to 14 only; closed since Sept. 15
going_out.item: Closed. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m., reads flounder, all species, Sept. 1 to 14 open and Sept. 15 to 30 closed, unlawful to possess, and carries no October opening; the proclamation it links, FF-27-2026, which the server delivered as a PDF (HTTP 200) and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, was signed June 3 by director Kathy B. Rawls and says it is unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 until 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14, 2026, with a 15-inch minimum and one per person per day inside that window, supersedes FF-17-2026 of March 13 and sets no later season. The division's proclamations index, six pages read at 5:50 a.m., carries nothing issued Oct. 21 or 22; the October flounder proclamations on it, FF-42-2026 of Oct. 6, FF-43-2026 of Oct. 13 and FF-44-2026 of Oct. 15, are commercial pound net and mobile gear orders, and there is no recreational one. Flounder in Topsail Sound are release only, the 38th day of the closure; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 21 days old today, has them as bycatch on red drum rigs and in the pier bottom-fishing catch.

waters.read: 208 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Down 46 cfs and 0.16 feet on the day against Wednesday's edition reading of 254 cfs and 2.27 feet, a fifth straight falling morning, and the recession is slowing: Wednesday's drop was 70, Tuesday's 97. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "208 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.", and the band is right by eight: the fetcher's pushy band runs 200 to 500 cfs and the river sits 8 cfs above the 200-cfs line where its long-leader, small-fly water begins. The fetcher's 321 cfs and 2.47 feet 24h_ago fields match the 5:45 a.m. Tuesday point on Wednesday's trace, not a point 24 hours old, so the 113-cfs drop they imply overstates the day; the falling flags are right either way. At 208 and falling the Williams is an edges problem and not yet a long-leader one: the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure fish from the near bank and the inside seams, the middle is still not a crossing, which is the fetcher's wadeable-at-the-edges line, and the water clears another day on a recession this steady. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage the file records, so a weighted stonefly nymph, size 8 to 10, on point with a caddis pupa dropper under an indicator, one split shot, worked up the inside seams and the soft water in each plunge pool's tail-out from the near bank; an olive or black weighted sculpin on a sink tip swung along the undercut banks and through the plunge pools where the current drops off; and with the flow eight cfs off the 200-cfs line, a size 14 to 16 caddis dry over the pocket water's softer seams in the afternoon. The Williams River in Pocahontas and Webster counties is on WVDNR's fall trout stocking schedule, code F in the 2026 Fishing Regulations Summary, one stocking each week for two weeks beginning the third Monday of October, which was Monday, Oct. 19, the program WTAP reported Monday as about 40,000 pounds of trout at nearly 40 waters over the weeks of Oct. 19 and 26; the Cranberry River and the Summersville Lake tailwaters carry the same code, and WVDNR's fish-stocking page, which posts stockings by the end of each business day, listed none when opened this morning, so no delivery to the Williams is confirmed. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed.

At normal pool the river fishes the structure and the current it makes, not the slack: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks; a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger; crawfish are the third forage the file records, so a crawfish-colored jig in the riprap for the smallmouth; and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark. The swings grow each day toward the spring tides, harder current through the inlet and more bait moving: today's sound flood is 3.1 feet, 0.8 to 3.9, against Wednesday's 3.0, and the evening ebb drains 3.3 feet to the day's lower low, 0.6 feet, which falls after midnight at 12:25 a.m. Friday and carries the file's spillover tag. NWS Wilmington has nothing on the beach or the water at Topsail this morning: the only product in the area is a Coastal Flood Advisory for Inland New Hanover, the lower Cape Fear River and downtown Wilmington, 6 to 9 a.m., issued 2:20 a.m., up to half a foot of water in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, which stops at the county line; Coastal Pender carried no active product at 5:45 a.m., a third morning, and Wednesday's Small Craft Advisory off the beach has expired. The sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.6 feet at 5:37 a.m., is on its ebb at press time, draining 2.8 feet to a 0.8-foot low at 11:59 a.m., then fills 3.1 feet to a 3.9-foot high at 6:03 p.m. and drains 3.3 feet to the 0.6-foot low at 12:25 a.m. Friday. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 4:57 a.m. at 4.3, low 11:01 a.m. at 0.8, high 5:16 p.m. at 4.6 and low 11:23 p.m. at 0.6, a 3.8-foot flood and a 4.0-foot ebb against Wednesday's 3.4 and 3.6. Today's lags from the two tables are 40 and 47 minutes on the highs and 58 and 62 minutes on the lows; the lows again lag longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 65.1 degrees at 5:30 a.m., up 0.9 from Wednesday's 64.2, a second morning up after three falling; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is a monthly report on its last morning inside the gate, not today's conditions: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, 21 days ago, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:45 this morning; Coastal Angler's newest Topsail report is Sept. 1, 51 days old, and is not used. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, inshore red drum the main target and no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jr. topwaters and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp soft plastics under popping corks, flounder as bycatch; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings 8 to 12 miles out. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the sound is on its morning ebb until 11:59 a.m., 54 minutes later than Wednesday's, and the last two hours of it, about 10 a.m. to noon, are the red drum stage in full daylight, finger mullet the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the ICWW channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low; the report's first-hour topwater for trout, a Spook Jr. walked over the deeper grass edges, falls on the top of the ebb just after first light. The flood from 11:59 a.m. to 6:03 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges, mud minnows and shrimp the forage there, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they go under, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead, the report's three- to four-pounders, and for spot, the calendar's October peak, a two-hook bottom rig with bloodworm or shrimp bits on the channel edges on the same flood. The 6:03 p.m. high puts 3.9 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 4 to 6 p.m., the dusk trout window riding the same high, then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the evening ebb, roughly 10:30 p.m. to the 12:25 a.m. Friday low, 45 minutes later than Wednesday's and in the dark, the same Carolina-rigged mullet and cut mullet at the channel edges; Beaufort's thermometer at 65.1 is up two mornings running, so the cool-down the guides in the report say the trout are waiting on is not on the gauge yet, and a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb, then the dock lights toward the 12:25 a.m. low, is the trout program the report describes. Oysters are in their eighth day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side has no product today; the piers' Gotcha-plug Spanish bite on the flood to the 5:16 p.m. high, 4.6 feet at the pier, and the evening cut-bait session for slot reds fall inside the moderate rip current risk and 2- to 4-foot surf the Wilmington surf zone forecast gives Coastal Pender. Slack at 11:59 a.m., 6:03 p.m. and 12:25 a.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only, the 38th day.
